questions.q: How can AI help with negative reviews?
questions.a: AI spots negative reviews the moment they're posted and flags the ones that need attention first. It can route each complaint to the right store or regional manager, alert them with context and suggest a personalized reply. That lets your team respond in minutes instead of finding the review days later in a weekly report.

questions.q: How quickly should a restaurant respond to a bad review?
questions.a: As quickly as you can, ideally within a day. The post cites ReviewTrackers research showing that businesses that respond to negative reviews within 24 hours see a higher customer return rate. A fast reply catches the guest while they still care about the outcome, before the issue snowballs on public platforms.

questions.q: What is a customer recovery workflow?
questions.a: A customer recovery workflow is the set of steps you follow to win back an unhappy guest. It usually covers detecting the complaint, routing it to the right person, sending a personal reply and making a recovery offer such as a refund, coupon or apology call. Tracking the outcome closes the loop, so you can see which guests returned.

questions.q: Can a fast response get a customer to change their review?
questions.a: Often, yes. When a guest feels heard and gets a fair resolution quickly, many update their review or come back. In the post's café example, a quick personal message and a free breakfast voucher led the guest to raise their rating and praise the fast response.

questions.q: What do I need to set up AI-powered review recovery across locations?
questions.a: You'll need a system that pulls in reviews from every platform in real time and uses sentiment analysis to flag priority issues. Add routing rules by store, region or issue type, plus recovery templates so every location responds consistently. Finally, track outcomes so you know which recoveries worked.
